title: Construct optimal unbiased reversible phase rounding (no κ)
body:
## Summary

Scoped all-lattice construction and proof with a finite exact certificate. Five explicit bijections of Z^2 give unbiased rounding of `A=[[3,-4],[4,3]]/5`. Retaining the uniform five-state seed gives an exact two-sided inverse. The expected squared error is zero when Ax is integral and `2/5` otherwise, the pointwise minimum among all unbiased integer-valued random outputs. Every individual map has squared error at most `4/5`.

```text
x = 5q + r
choose uniform s independently of x
F_s(x) = Bq + table_s[r], B=5A
inverse: identify output coset, subtract its table point, apply B^-1
```

The new step is an unbiased reversible ensemble attaining the unconstrained stochastic error optimum. Dependent coordinate weights form a five-regular input/output coset graph; five exact matchings give the witness. Classical scalar rounding variance, lattice quotients and matching decomposition retain their credit. This contribution was produced by Nick Petalas.

The original card is explicitly changed to a generic precision-interface result. No new kappa, selected-frontier change or complete multiplication theorem is claimed. The investigation stopped at this first verified construction.

## Evidence

Before this construction, coordinatewise independent stochastic rounding has the correct means and minimum scalar errors, but fails the output-coset capacity condition in this quotient. The new dependent ensemble preserves every output coset in each seed and attains the same pointwise error optimum.

Local CPython 3.12.15, standard library only:

- All 125 seed/residue entries pass exact output-transversal, first-moment, nearest-cell and squared-error checks. Translation covariance and the explicit inverse prove the all-lattice statement.
- 16,810 signed two-sided roundtrips, 3,750 larger-quotient images, 1,250 signed translation cases through 1,024-bit coordinates and five semantic controls pass.
- Warning-strict normal and optimized direct commands pass, locally timed at 0.03135 and 0.02878 seconds. These are replay-deadline measurements, not speedup claims. Both registered commands pass; the complete registered command took 0.28834 seconds.
- Metadata/source pins, in-memory syntax checks, staged whitespace, committed bytes/source history and official eight-file export integrity pass at `b07ae963075920c46a1662b6d1297dbfa3e6dc16`.
- Both modes pass in a read-only Git-free export with empty PATH. All nine exported files, including the export receipt, retain their bytes. Generated replay receipts bind all eight package-file hashes. No receipt is handwritten and no optimizer is required for replay.

From the repository root:

```sh
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -W error -B research/unbiased-periodic-rotation/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -O -W error -B research/unbiased-periodic-rotation/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/unbiased-periodic-rotation
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/unbiased-periodic-rotation --check-source-history
```

Any CPython 3.12 path may substitute. Expected scientific marker: `PASS_UNBIASED_PERIODIC_ROTATION`.

## Limitations

Exact return retains the externally supplied seed. Sampling, seed storage/entropy recovery, reversible quotient lookup, bounded-word arithmetic and physical tape costs remain unpriced. Input independence of the seed is required. No inverse-unbiasedness, adaptive seed reuse, repeated-word error, selected-root/caller binding, native implementation or favorable complete recursive invoice is proved. The maps allow outward norm movement. All five framework assumptions remain. Selected cold replay, native builds, Lean, Docker, independent human review and formal proof-kernel review are unrun or unclaimed.

The same rational phase occurs in ywz65's PR2589 and Nick Petalas's PR6304. Their deterministic lifting and tie-rule results are context, not premises or audit targets. This result changes the numerical contract to unbiased random output; it claims no smaller deterministic all-grid error threshold. No predecessor scientific suite was rerun.

## Open next questions

- Bind a supplier phase, input/output lattice and seed ownership, then price sampling, lookup and restoration at an actual caller. The missing physical contract and complete invoice are blockers.
- Determine which other rational orthogonal operators admit unbiased nearest-cell periodic bijection ensembles. Start with exact quotient capacities and moment constraints; no general existence theorem or extension is reserved.

## Related open work

- [PR6418](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6418) bounds adaptive bias from a reused rounding seed. This ensemble requires an independent input/seed and gives no reuse guarantee; no shared numerical instance is computed.
- [PR4017](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/4017) supplies a source-bound reversible native macro with dirty scratch. This contribution supplies a generic stochastic planar lattice interface and no competing macro cost or source-specific error value.
- [PR6429](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6429) bounds integer temporaries for once-rounded rational gates. The present proof concerns a five-seed output distribution and its inverses, with no competing temporary-width claim.
